purpose: This vaccine protects you from Tick-Borne Encephalitis (TBE), a serious brain infection caused by a virus spread through tick bites. It is recommended if you live in, work in, or plan to travel to areas where TBE is common, such as parts of Europe and Asia. Getting vaccinated is one of the best ways to protect yourself, especially if you spend time outdoors in wooded or grassy areas.
how_it_works: The vaccine contains a killed (inactivated) form of the TBE virus, which cannot cause infection. When it is injected into your body, your immune system recognizes it as a threat and builds up defenses against it. This means if you are ever exposed to the real virus through a tick bite, your body is already prepared to fight it off quickly.
common_side_effects: Most people feel fine after the vaccine. The most common side effects are a sore, red, or swollen arm where the shot was given. Some people feel tired, get a mild headache, have muscle aches, or run a low fever for a day or two. These are normal signs that your immune system is responding and they usually go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you have ever had a severe allergic reaction to a previous dose of this vaccine or any of its ingredients. If you have a weakened immune system or take medications that suppress your immune system, let your healthcare provider know before getting vaccinated. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should discuss the risks and benefits with their doctor before receiving this vaccine. Seek emergency help right away if you experience difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, rapid heartbeat, or dizziness after the injection.
typical_dosing: The basic protection schedule involves 3 doses. The second dose is given 1 to 3 months after the first, and the third dose is given 5 to 12 months after the second. A booster dose is usually recommended every 3 to 5 years if you remain at risk. There is also a faster schedule available if you need protection sooner, so talk to your doctor about the best option for you.
